evidence.note: Repeatedly searched for a zstd/zstdcat binary and attempted apt-get install zstd to enable differential comparison; never found one, so byte-exact comparison against `zstd -d` was never realized — the intent for differential testing existed but was unfulfilled.
Leaned on the provided /app/test.sh as the main correctness gate across the run, re-running it after fixes.

Wrote custom C diagnostic programs (analyze.c, parse_tables.c, verify_fse.c, etc.) to inspect block structure and cross-check generated FSE tables against RFC Appendix A golden values, isolating which subsystem was faulty — verification beyond test.sh, but tied to the RFC rather than a reference decoder.

Searched for .ref/.expected reference files; none existed, and no own-generated .zst corpus was created. All checks stayed on the handful of provided test_artifacts, focused on repetitive.zst; no feature-matrix coverage (FCS widths, treeless, dictionary) was exercised.

reasoning: The agent clearly went beyond the level-3 anchor of relying solely on test.sh: it built self-authored diagnostic C harnesses and cross-checked internal FSE tables against RFC Appendix A golden values to isolate failing subsystems. But it never achieved the level-5 behavior of diffing decoder output against `zstd -d` on new inputs — the reference binary was unavailable and it could not generate its own .zst corpus, so all verification stayed confined to the provided handful of files and one target file. This places it between the 3 and 5 anchors, at 4.
